reason: The visible NN assembly has a concrete bottleneck candidate: each 64×64 output block extracts and stores ZA0/ZA1, then ZA2/ZA3, with stores advancing through C in column-major order. The proposal changes this to complete the two row pairs in sequence while preserving selectors and destinations. That may affect write locality, but the supplied evidence does not establish a timing benefit. Correctness risk is limited to matching each extracted tile to its existing destination and overwriting every output once. The prior FMOPA-order experiment measured no repeatable gain; no measurements are supplied for this store-order change. It is the only board experiment ID, so it ranks first.
